text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Thursday.

LONDON - Stocks ended little changed after a rally on Wall Street bucked up prices depressed by worries over a jump in inflation. The FTSE 100 fell 0.8 points to 3,926.1 after falling as low as 3,904 earlier in the session.

FRANKFURT - Shares shrugged off an early bout of profit-taking to end higher, boosted by gains in the banking sector and continuing a rally begun on Tuesday. The blue-chip DAX index rose 3.58 points to 2,777.01 and stood at 2,784.39 in after-hours electronic trading.
PARIS - Stocks were little changed after briefly touching a high for the year in heavy trading led by shares of insurers UAP and Axa. The blue-chip CAC-40 index rose 0.99 points to 2,218.18.

ZURICH - Shares set a record high after an early boost in the financial sector and a late dollar rally pushed prices ahead. Dealers said investor interest was focused on financials, cyclicals and consumer stocks. The broad SPI index gained 19.66 points to 2,463.63.

TOKYO - Stocks edged higher. Participants remained sidelined as even a slew of corporate earnings results failed to serve as an incentive, brokers said, adding that the government's package of financial deregulation measures would take time to implement. The key Nikkei 225 average rose 51.60 points to close at 21,031.04.
HONG KONG - The Hang Seng Index closed above 13,000 points for the first time, driven by optimism about interest rates and the property market. The index rose 61.11 points to 13,004.80.
SYDNEY - Stocks scored solid gains, boosted by strength in shares of gold producers and other metals firms. The All Ordinaries index closed up 15.6 points at 2,362.5.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares rose on perceptions that recent heavy selling, which has wiped almost 3 percent off the market's value this month, was overdone. The overall index rose 60.6 points to 6,815.9, the industrial index added 66.1 points to 7,980.2 and the gold index gained 31.7 points to 1,743.6.
